OSCAL specifies that when a link's href should point to another object within the same document, it must use a URI fragment — a relative reference made up only of a hash sign followed by the identifier or UUID of the target object. As stated in the uri-use documentation: [Q1]. The data type for such fields is uri-reference, and the approach is described as a locator. A concrete example given in that same source is: [Q2]. This is consistent with the general identifier-referencing guidance in the layer-overview, which states: [Q3]. The 'effective data model' referenced in Q1 also includes objects from any directly or transitively imported documents, so the same fragment syntax works across composed instances — not just within a single file.

Check that every same-document href in your OSCAL file starts with '#' and that the value following '#' exactly matches the id or uuid attribute of the target element. The validator can confirm whether those fragment values resolve to a declared object in the document's effective data model.
